newsitem.title: UK: UK court upholds Lloyd's debt collection rulings.
newsitem.headline: UK court upholds Lloyd's debt collection rulings.

text.p: The Lloyd's of London insurance market said Britain's court of appeal upheld on Thursday, its right to take action against its backers who failed to pay outstanding debts due for its reconstruction plan announced in September 1996.

The Appeal court upheld two high court judgements made in Lloyd's favour in February and April, thereby removing the final defences made by Lloyd's members against Lloyd's ability to collect outstanding debt, said Lloyd's of London in a statement.
The appeal court refused leave to appeal to the House of Lords and awarded Lloyd's its costs of the appeal proceedings, said Lloyd's.

Philip Holden, head of Lloyd's financial recovery department, said: "This will give added impetus to our increasingly successful debt collection strategy. We have issued over 1400 writs, obtained 223 judgements to date and have now issued applications for summary judgement against all those who have net yet settled their debts to Lloyd's."
